sentences.text: Dr. Anjali Gyanani-Public Prosecutor for respondent/Sta Heard on I.A.No.15562/2025, third repeat repeat application under Section 389(1) Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of sole appellant - Shashank Dohaliya.

Appellant is facing sentence by virtue of judgment dated 14/01/2023 passed by Sixth Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Bhind (M.P.) in ST No.100/2021; whereby, he has been convicted and sentenced as under:-
 Section Imprisonment F  376-AB of IPC 20 Years' R.I. Rs.10,000/-
 stipu  5(M)/6 of POCSO 20 Years' R.I. Rs.10,000/-
 Act stipu

entities.text: Sixth Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Bhind (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is the submission of counsel for appellants that trial Court erred in convicting and awarding jail sentence to appellant.
He already suffered around 3 years and 10 months of incarceration as pre and post trial confinement.

As per allegations, appellant used finger to commit offence but medical report of victim belies the allegations and testimony of Dr. Babita Ahirwar (PW-7) indicates that no injury was sustained by victim who was 6 year old girl over her person including private part.
It is highly improbable that if such act would have been done, then medical report does not indicate any sign of injury or hurt over private part of victim.
This makes the case of prosecution vulnerable.
It was a case of monetary dispute which was tried to be converted into such offence.
Appellant is running a tuition class and when money was asked from parents of the victim, then these allegations were levelled.
It is a motivated case against appellant.
Moreover, appellant has good case on merits and hearing of appeal shall take some time.
Fine amount has already been deposited.
He undertakes to abide by the terms and conditions as imposed by this Court.
Under such circumstances, learned counsel for appellants prays for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant.

sentences.text: Per contra, counsel for respondent/State opposed the application and prayed for its dismissal.
Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.
Considering the arguments advanced by counsel for the parties, this Court intends to allow the application for suspension of sentence (I.A.No.15562/2025).

If appellant - Shashank Dohaliya furnishes bail bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) along with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court that he shall appear before the Principal Registrar of this Court on 11/11/2025 and thereafter,
on all other subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Office for appearance, then he shall be released on bail and execution of jail sentence is suspended till disposal of this appeal, subject to deposit of fine amount.
I.A.No.15562/2025 stands disposed of, accordingly.
The appellant shall mark his presence before concerned Police Station on first Sunday of every month between 10:30 am to 2:00 pm for the next two years i.e. till September, 2027.
The appellant shall not be source of embarrassment and harassment to the complainant/victim side and her family member in any manner.

He shall not move in their vicinity and will not try to contact them in person/through somebody else or through electronic media; otherwise, benefit of bail given today by way of suspension of sentence shall be withdrawn immediately.
A copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance and information.
Certified copy as per rules/directions.
(ANAND PATHAK) (PU  JUDGE
(Dubey)
